belief: “I’ve earned it. After what I’ve been through, I deserve the relief.”
belief_plain: I’ve earned it. After what I’ve been through, I deserve the relief
origins: If you have suffered, relief can feel like something you are owed. A hard childhood, a loss, a body in pain, a mind that will not rest: of course you want the pain to stop. Wanting relief is not selfish. The lie is narrower. It says this particular use is the relief you have earned, and that you should not question it because of what you have been through. You can honor the pain and still tell the truth that this kind of relief is hurting you. God is not stingy with comfort. He does not say you must keep hurting. He offers rest that does not master you. If you want help, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. Do not try to stop or withdraw on your own if that could make you sick. A doctor can help you do it safely, and a counselor can walk with you. Needing that help is not a failure.
self: After what I have been through, I deserve this.
Anyone in my place would use.
If I stop, I am refusing myself the only kindness I get.
God does not understand how tired I am.
Comfort that comes with a cost is still mine to keep.
People who tell me to get help do not know what I have survived.
replacement: I am allowed to want relief after what I have been through. Using is not the only comfort God has for me.
